text:
Sam: Quick heads-up — I ran the replay harness this morning comparing the old kernel selector (v1) vs the new latency-aware heuristic (v2). Seeing p99 tail regressions on mixed-tenant traces, esp when small low-latency requests interleave with large long-context batches.

Priya: ugh. Are the runs apples-to-apples? same model binary, same quantization, cache state? :thinking:

Jordan: Yes — pinned same model hash + quant (int8), identical runtime flags, disabled autoscaling, and we used two modes: (1) synthetic Poisson arrivals, (2) replayed production traces with inter-arrival jitter preserved. KV cache behavior was toggled for a set of runs to isolate eviction effects.

Sam: Profiling highlights: GPU SM util ~72% on average, p50 ~18ms, p95 ~84ms, p99 ~210ms for v2. v1 had p99 ~150ms on the same trace. CPU queuing shows long head-of-line waits when tenant A's big sequences occupy batching window.

Kai: Can you paste the replay harness config you used? Curious about batch caps and max_delay settings.

Sam: Here — minimal snippet from the harness config we used for the comparison:
```
# replay-harness.yaml
model_hash: rwl-model-3b-int8
arrival_mode: replay
preserve_jitter: true
batching:
  max_delay_ms: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_batch_items: 64
  per_tenant_token_cap: 4096
kernel_selector: latency_aware_v2
trace_pinning: false
```

Lina: That max_delay_ms=8 seems large for tiny requests — could allow one big request to delay a bunch of small ones and inflate tail. Have you tried 2–4ms?

Sam: Not yet on replay traces. I ran a synthetic sweep: with max_delay_ms=4 p99 dropped ~25% for small-request tenants but small decrease in GPU throughput. Tradeoff is higher per-token cost.

Jordan: Also noticed KV cache: when we enable prefix caching, tenants with repeated short prefixes got dramatic p50 improvements but caused cache pressure leading to extra evictions for other tenants with large contexts. Evictions correlate with higher p99 on those tenants.

Priya: So there are two interacting systems: batching window and KV eviction policy. For apples-to-apples, we should control for cache state in at least one baseline (cold cache) and one warmed baseline.

Kai: Agreed. Proposed experiment matrix:
- baseline cold cache + v1 selector
- warmed cache + v1 selector
- cold cache + v2 selector
- warmed cache + v2 selector
All with (a) replay traces and (b) synthetic interleaved tenants (random shuffle). That should show selector fairness differences.

Lina: For fairness metrics, let's add per-tenant median_wait, p95_wait, tokens_queued_over_time, and starved_tenant_count (tenants with >X% requests blocked >Yms). Also compute effective_tokens_per_second per tenant and normalized fairness index.

Sam: Good list. I also want to try a tenant-shuffle experiment where we randomize the enqueue order to avoid deterministic bias from tenant ordering in the scheduler. That unblocked a lot of pathological cases previously.

ops-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout kernel-selector/latency_aware_v2 -> eng-runtime canary (deployed at 2026-03-15T09:12Z).

Priya: One quick micro-optimization idea: enforce a soft per-tenant dequeue cap per batch (e.g., at most 25% of batch tokens from any single tenant) to limit head-of-line dominance. Might reduce throughput marginally but improve tail fairness.

Jordan: Here's a sample log excerpt showing the bottleneck pattern (simplified):
[2026-03-15T09:22:01Z] batch_id=4532 size_tokens=1830 tenants={A:1600, B:100, C:130} delay_ms=7 kernel=latency_aware_v2
[2026-03-15T09:22:01Z] tenant B req_id=... wait_ms=120 p99
[2026-03-15T09:22:01Z] batch_id=4533 size_tokens=1972 tenants={A:1800, C:172} delay_ms=8

Lina: That exactly shows A hogging batches. Let's try introducing per-batch tenant token limits and a small max_delay_ms=3 test on replay traces. If it improves p99 for B/C with <5% throughput loss, we should consider as a heuristic.

Sam: I'll run the full matrix: replay vs synthetic, shuffled vs ordered, cache cold/warm, max_delay sweep [2,4,8], per-tenant token cap sweep [15%,25%,40%]. Expected run time ~6 hours per full matrix. Kicking off now. Will post perf dashboards and raw traces when done.

Kai: Thanks — if you can include the exact kernel timings (ms per kernel) and allocation/eviction counts from KV store that'd help root cause. Also tag me @Kai when results land. :white_check_mark:

Priya: One more note — for apples-to-apples we should pin the same RNG seed in replay harness and disable any adaptive batching randomness. Small nondeterminism caused confusing diffs earlier.

Sam: Good call. I'll pin seeds and disable batching randomness. Back in a few hours with results.

Lina: Thanks — and please add a short summary (1-2 bullets) with recommendations at the top of the results thread so product/ops can act quickly.
